slice: Pre-build review of the complete, member-readable Werkles tech-stack runway.
sharedContext: The current static catalog covers Supabase Auth/Postgres/Storage, Stripe Billing/Identity, Plaid, Twilio Verify, and Checkr.
Werkles Constitution and pricing canon also name PostHog analytics and Expo Push as infrastructure vendors, but the catalog and Crucible journey omit them.
Vercel hosts the app and 1Password holds operator secrets; those are operator/runtime infrastructure, not member-facing verification features.
Every current slot has one narrow purpose, a non-live stage, a blocker, an authority boundary, and a planned data-minimization statement.
No provider activation, credentials, schema, SQL, tracking, notification send, push, or deploy is in scope.
liveStrings: One member journey. Different tools for different jobs.
A provider name never means trusted.
Not live yet: what would happen to the data
Only checks labeled available can be started.
knownGaps: PostHog and Expo Push are canonical vendors but have no catalog slot, adapter, route, member state, or data boundary.
The current journey does not distinguish member-facing services from hosting and secret custody.
A destination link is required by the current type even when a future service has no member page.

BEAN.vision: Prevent analytics and notifications from becoming surveillance or implied consent when they enter the catalog.
BEAN.pull: Attack proposed PostHog and Expo Push boundaries for unnecessary collection, cross-context tracking, sensitive inference, retention ambiguity, notification leakage, and dishonest readiness claims.
go: State whether each vendor belongs in the member journey at all.
Give the minimum safe Werkles-keeps, provider-handles, deletion/expiry, and consent language for each.
Name any wording or state that must block implementation.
BEAN.momentum: Give one fail-closed regression for analytics and one for push notifications.
BEAN.outOfLane: No implementation, provider call, live research, credentials, schema, SQL, activation, push, deploy, send, secrets, or spend.

COMPUTER.vision: Make the stack map complete and commercially legible without mixing product features, platform infrastructure, and future plans.
COMPUTER.pull: Review the proposed three-layer model: product/runtime, member-facing providers, operator custody. Attack omissions and category mistakes from supplied source only.
go: Classify Next.js/React, Vercel, Supabase, 1Password, Stripe Billing, Stripe Identity, Plaid, Twilio Verify, Checkr, PostHog, and Expo Push into the right layer.
Decide the best member-readable placement and readiness label for PostHog and Expo Push.
Name two narrow improvements that add real integration readiness instead of dashboard theater.
COMPUTER.momentum: Give one concise stack list Ben can use in a vendor conversation.
COMPUTER.outOfLane: No implementation, visual claim, live research, provider call, credentials, schema, SQL, activation, push, deploy, send, secrets, spend, or new vendor.
